newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Japanese firm to invest $17 mln in S.Lanka-paper.
newsitem.headline: Japanese firm to invest $17 mln in S.Lanka-paper.

text.p: A Japanese firm will invest at least 100 million rupees ($17 million) in an electronics factory in Sri Lanka, the independent Island said on Saturday.
The newspaper said the first phase of the plant, owned by a unit of Tosslec Co Ltd of Kyoto, Japan, was opened on Friday at Biyagama, five km (two miles) east of the capital Colombo.
The plant would manufacture a range of components, including lithium batteries for cellular phones, printed circuit boards for cameras, liquid crystal displays, small motors, and coils.
The factory, involving an initial investment of $10 million, would employ up to 1,200 people by the end of 1998, Jitsuo Misaka, the chairman and director was quoted as saying.
The total investment would be around $17 million "only in respect of equipment", he added.

From September the local company, Toslanka Co (Pvt) Ltd, would export to Japanese markets through several companies, including Matsushita and Mitsubishi, one of the local directors, was quoted as saying by the newspaper.
